lines: The gear took the blow and stayed together.
I used it when the fighting reached the dock.
It kept the worst of that strike away from me.
The grip held even after my hands got wet.
I put it to work and came back with only scratches.
It carried its weight when trouble started.
The edge needs attention, but it did not fail me.
I trusted it once the arrows began falling.
It turned aside something that would have reached my ribs.
The straps held through the whole fight.
I used every part of it except the buckle I was worried about.
It is scuffed now for a good reason.
The balance felt right when I had no time to think.
It earned a proper cleaning after what we survived.
I would take it into danger again.
The gear stayed firm when I was knocked against the rail.
It gave me enough confidence to hold my place.
One hard hit bent it slightly, but not enough to matter then.
I came home because good equipment did its share.
It worked. That is the best report I can give.
Dry, unused, and welcome. Some gear should stay out of danger.
I never had to draw it.
The fighting ended before I needed the gear.
It stayed packed through the whole trip.
I checked it afterward and found no damage.
We carried it for caution, not because trouble reached us.
The gear came home exactly as it left.
I was glad to have it and happier not to use it.
It never left its straps.
No blood, no dents, and no repairs needed.
The weapon stayed sheathed from the first mile to the last.
I kept it close, but the road remained quiet.
It was ready when we needed caution and unnecessary when we reached safety.
The armor never took a hit.
I did not test it in combat this time.
It stayed clean apart from road dust.
The gear was insurance on a journey that went well.
Nobody forced me to find out how strong it was.
I will store it until the next trip.
Unused gear and a safe return make a fine pair.
